question.prompt: An equilateral triangle and a regular hexagon have equal perimeters. If the area of the triangle is \(2,\) then the area of the hexagon is:

solutions.explanation:
Compare the figures by dividing them into equilateral triangles of the same size. Let \(s>0\) be the hexagon's side length. Its perimeter is \(6s\), so the equilateral triangle with the same perimeter has side length \(2s\).

Join the three side midpoints of the triangle. Each joining segment is parallel to the third side and half its length. Thus the triangle splits into four congruent equilateral triangles of side \(s\). Since their total area is \(2\), each has area
\[
\frac24=\frac12.
\]
Next join the center of the regular hexagon to its six vertices. This divides it into six isosceles triangles, each with central angle \(360^\circ/6=60^\circ\). Its two remaining angles are also \(60^\circ\), so each piece is equilateral with side \(s\).

These six pieces fill the hexagon with no overlapping interiors. Each has area \(\tfrac12\), so the hexagon's area is
\[
6\cdot\frac12=\boxed{3},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Divide both shapes into equal pieces
